definition: In linguistics, aggregation is a subtask of natural language generation, which involves merging syntactic constituents (such as sentences and phrases) together.
details: Sometimes aggregation can be done at a conceptual level.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. Boil it down and it is this: In linguistics, aggregation is a subtask of natural language generation, which involves merging syntactic constituents (such as sentences and phrases) together. Here is why it matters: Sometimes aggregation can be done at a conceptual level. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. That pattern-earned fluency is Aggregation (linguistics).
